findings.description: Test-ContinuousCoReviewPathUnderRoot uses OrdinalIgnoreCase only on Windows and Ordinal on every POSIX host. Get-ContinuousCoReviewPhysicalPath also preserves caller spelling for ordinary components. On a case-insensitive macOS volume, `/Users/.../repo` and `/users/.../repo` can therefore name the same directory but compare as different, so New-GitReviewTargetSnapshot can accept an explicitly supplied case-aliased ExternalRoot that is physically inside the origin. That violates the external disposable-worktree containment guarantee. The same OS shortcut in reviewed-state-digest.ps1:92 also fails to strip case-variant machinery on such a volume. Determine case semantics from the actual volume/Git worktree rather than the OS family, and cover both case-insensitive and case-sensitive macOS volumes.
findings.title: Case-insensitive macOS volumes can bypass external-worktree containment

findings.description: Get-ContinuousCoReviewMachineryPaths finishes with `Sort-Object -Unique`, whose default comparison is case-insensitive. On a case-sensitive Linux or macOS worktree containing two non-ignored marker-detected machinery directories whose names differ only by case, one path is discarded before the digest builds its strip patterns. Files under the discarded directory then remain in the frozen candidate even though both directories are classified as machinery. Use a comparer that follows the actual worktree's case semantics and add a fixture where both case-distinct marker directories are non-ignored.
findings.title: Case-insensitive deduplication drops distinct machinery paths on case-sensitive worktrees

findings.description: Marker-detected machinery paths are literal repository identities, but the digest appends them directly to the denylist and Test-ContinuousCoReviewDigestPathDenied evaluates non-subtree entries as WildcardPattern values. A legal machinery directory name containing wildcard metacharacters can therefore match and remove an unrelated reviewable source path (for example, machinery `generated[1]` also matches a root source file named `generated1`), leaving that source outside the reviewed tree identity. The same frozen paths are later passed to Git pathspec-taking commands without literal escaping. Keep machinery identities separate from user exclusion globs and pass them to Git with literal pathspec semantics.
findings.title: Literal machinery paths are interpreted as wildcard pathspecs

summary: Risk-based review completed. Both controller-declared verification commands succeeded against the exact target digest, but the candidate retains one blocking cross-platform containment defect and two major candidate-membership defects in machinery path handling.
